title: Boss: the TLS help desk
summary: Tickets arrive with broken certificates. Diagnose each one, then fix the code that issued them.

steps.title: Your queue
body: You are on the TLS help desk. Every test certificate comes from `DojoCert`-style helpers: ECDSA P-256, valid 2030 to 2035
unless a ticket says otherwise. "Now" is 1 June 2031 UTC. The namespaces are imported.

steps.title: Full diagnosis
prompt: Write `string Diagnose(X509Certificate2 leaf, List<X509Certificate2> sent, X509Certificate2 trustedRoot, string host)`.
Build an `X509Chain` (custom root trust with `trustedRoot`, `sent` as extra certificates, serverAuth `ApplicationPolicy`
`1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1`, no revocation check, verification time 2031-06-01 UTC) and return the **first** problem found:
starter: string Diagnose(X509Certificate2 leaf, List<X509Certificate2> sent, X509Certificate2 trustedRoot, string host)
solution: string Diagnose(X509Certificate2 leaf, List<X509Certificate2> sent, X509Certificate2 trustedRoot, string host)
hints: Check the chain statuses in order first; check the hostname only when the chain has no problems.
template: var dojoInter = DojoCert("CN=Issuing CA", dojoRoot, true);
Dojo.Eq("ticket 1: all good", "ok", Diagnose(dojoLeaf, new() { dojoInter }, dojoRoot, "www.shop.example"));
Dojo.Eq("ticket 2: server forgot the chain file", "missing intermediate", Diagnose(dojoLeaf, new(), dojoRoot, "shop.example"));
Dojo.Eq("ticket 3: a look-alike root is trusted, not the real one", "untrusted root", Diagnose(dojoLeaf, new() { dojoInter, dojoRoot }, dojoOtherRoot, "shop.example"));
Dojo.Eq("ticket 4: expired at New Year", "expired", Diagnose(dojoOld, new() { dojoInter }, dojoRoot, "old.example"));
Dojo.Eq("ticket 5: clientAuth certificate on a web server", "wrong purpose", Diagnose(dojoClient, new() { dojoInter }, dojoRoot, "shop.example"));
Dojo.Eq("ticket 6: new hostname, old certificate", "wrong name", Diagnose(dojoLeaf, new() { dojoInter }, dojoRoot, "api.shop.example"));
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);

steps.title: Fix the issuing code
prompt: This method is supposed to issue a server certificate for `host`, signed by `issuer` (which has its private key),
but every certificate it makes fails the help desk's diagnosis. Find and fix **three** mistakes so that
`Diagnose` from the last step would say `"ok"`:
- it must be valid for TLS **server** authentication,
starter: var req = new CertificateRequest("CN=" + host, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
solution: var req = new CertificateRequest("CN=" + host, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
hints: The CN isn't enough: modern clients only look at the SAN. Add one with `SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder`.
Not After is 2031-01-01: before "now". Push it past mid-2031 (but not past the issuer's own expiry in 2035).
template: var dojoInter = DojoCert("CN=Issuing CA", dojoRoot, true);
Dojo.Eq("has its private key", true, dojoIssued.HasPrivateKey);
Dojo.Eq("covers the host via SAN", true, dojoIssued.MatchesHostname("orders.contoso.test", allowCommonName: false));
Dojo.Check("chain validates for serverAuth on 2031-06-01", dojoOk, "chain status: " + string.Join(",", dojoChain.ChainStatus.Select(s => s.Status)));
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);
steps.explain: `MatchesHostname(..., allowCommonName: false)` is how browsers behave. By default .NET falls back to the CN when a certificate has no DNS SAN, which can hide this bug in .NET-only testing.

steps.title: Triage the whole fleet
prompt: The monitoring team sends a batch of `(host, leaf)` pairs, all served with the same `sent` intermediates and checked against `root`.

`Diagnose` from the last step is already in the editor. Using it, write `Dictionary<string, int> Triage(List<(string Host, X509Certificate2 Leaf)> fleet, List<X509Certificate2> sent, X509Certificate2 root)`
that counts how many hosts got each verdict. Only verdicts that occur appear as keys.
starter: // Diagnose from the last step (the reference version; replace it with yours if you like)
string Diagnose(X509Certificate2 leaf, List<X509Certificate2> sent, X509Certificate2 trustedRoot, string host)
Dictionary<string, int> Triage(List<(string Host, X509Certificate2 Leaf)> fleet, List<X509Certificate2> sent, X509Certificate2 root)
solution: string Diagnose(X509Certificate2 leaf, List<X509Certificate2> sent, X509Certificate2 trustedRoot, string host)
Dictionary<string, int> Triage(List<(string Host, X509Certificate2 Leaf)> fleet, List<X509Certificate2> sent, X509Certificate2 root)
string verdict = Diagnose(leaf, sent, root, host);
hints: Loop over the fleet, call `Diagnose` for each, and count.
template: var dojoInter = DojoCert("CN=Issuing CA", dojoRoot, true);

var dojoT = Triage(new List<(string Host, X509Certificate2 Leaf)> { ("a.example", dojoA), ("b.example", dojoB), ("c.example", dojoC), ("d.example", dojoD), ("www.a.example", dojoA) }, new() { dojoInter }, dojoRoot);
Dojo.Eq("verdicts found", new List<string> { "expired", "ok", "wrong name", "wrong purpose" }, dojoT.Keys.OrderBy(k => k).ToList());
Dojo.Eq("one on the wrong name", 1, dojoT.GetValueOrDefault("wrong name"));
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);
